lines.trans: Hello, Viktor Stepanovich, good day!
Hello, Pavel. What do you want?
That was a very subtle move!
I understood everything, thank you very much.
And is that all you will say?
Please forgive me for my foolishness.
And is that all?
You are a genius and the greatest mind of our time!
Enough, do not flatter too much.
Alright, keep fighting for power.
I will definitely win these elections!
Then work hard and do not relax.
Thank you for the support, Viktor Stepanovich!

meanings.note: Plural only. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'боры'). Common substantive noun meaning 'election' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Qualitative adjective. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'дающийся'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('outstanding, prominent').

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'играть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to win', paired with 'выигрывать'.

examples.text: Паша, эти выборы ты не выиграешь.

Firm promise or requirement. Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'язательно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'держка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'support, backing' in everyday Russian.

meanings.en: to fawn, suck up, flatter excessively
meanings.note: Colloquial reflexive verb. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'лизываться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to fawn, flatter', paired with 'подлизаться'.

examples.trans: There is no need to fawn before bosses.
Enough, do not flatter too much.

meanings.note: Handing something over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

Handing something over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Простите! = sorry! forgive me!. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.

Imperative: прости / простите. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.

meanings.en: to relax, let one's guard down
meanings.note: Reflexive imperfective verb. Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'слабляться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to relax', paired with 'расслабиться'.

meanings.note: Adverb of degree. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ильно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
